legend_scale_html: 2 m air temperature (degF), FIXED key (-60..150 F) with a STEADY gradient on the map: the raster blends smoothly through blue-white extreme cold → gray-blue subfreezing → royal-blue freezing wall (30-40) → frigid turquoise/blues (40-55) → transitional lime/teals (55-70) → mellow yellows (70-85) → warming orange/golds (85-100) → scorching pink/reds (100+) to HIGHEST+ 150, passing exactly through every key color (key bars show the LOWEST -60 to HIGHEST+ 150 band centers). Same temperature always shows the same color; every color is brightened so nothing renders dark. Freezing (32 F) sits inside the royal-blue wall.

na_bounds.note: Authoritative common geography for the four North American live layers (precipitation_na, air_temperature_na, cloud_cover_na, wind_na). Every NA builder bins its own source grid onto this exact canvas, so the four overlays align in Google Earth. Degrees per pixel: 0.05 x 0.05 (square). This boundary is a bounding extent enclosing the buffered landmass; it does not imply valid source data everywhere — areas without valid source data stay transparent.
